PullRequest.Title: Align Source Control resource decorations
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #158212 Source Control resource badges relied on each status letter's intrinsic glyph width and inherited vertical margins, making M/U/D/R appear uneven and visually misaligned. This gives resource decorations a shared 16×16 centered box with the standard label type role. Existing Git decoration colors, deleted-file strikethrough, tooltips, selection, and high-contrast behavior remain unchanged. A component fixture covers modified, untracked, deleted, and renamed states in all four core theme variants. ## Before / After
BeforeAfter
## Validation - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/scm/scmResourceDecorations.fixture.ts` - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/media/scm.css` - `npm run transpile-client` - Component fixture rendered without errors in light, dark, and high-contrast themes

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and scroll decorated Source Control resource rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each visible or newly recycled SCM row, existing resource-label rendering supplies the decoration badge; browser style resolution and layout of the row must complete before paint. The diff only changes the existing one-character ::after badge to a fixed 16x16 inline-flex box.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of visible decorated rows in the virtualized SCM list, not the total repository change count; each matching row contains one bounded single-character badge.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM style and layout run synchronously on the renderer main thread; list virtualization bounds simultaneous row layout to the viewport and overscan. The diff adds no task fan-out, queue, or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no new application cache or cache key. Warm scrolling reuses list row templates; recycled rows undergo the same existing label update, while the added CSS remains stylesheet-cached. Cold and warm paths introduce no extra data fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in path and cost shape from the SCM ResourceRenderer and scoped selector: the rule matches only existing decorated resource labels and performs constant bounded layout work per visible badge.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/layout cost varies by visible-row count and browser, but the new local flex container has one text child and fixed dimensions; no evidence supports a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is a local constant-size geometry change on already-rendered badges, without forced geometry reads, broad invalidation selectors, additional DOM nodes, repeated script work, or scaling boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the SCM resource-decoration component fixture across themes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture setup creates four rows and labels synchronously before screenshot capture; all four must render for the fixture to complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality of four decoration records and four DOM rows per fixture render; additional theme variants rerun this bounded test-only setup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four rows are constructed serially on the test renderer thread; theme fixture scheduling is controlled by the existing harness and the diff adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or bypassed. CSS/module loading follows the existing fixture harness, and each fixture render builds a fresh bounded DOM.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete added fixture: one four-element map, one four-element loop, no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Harness-level screenshot timing is not inspected, but the changed fixture's own work is statically bounded to four rows and one generated style element.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is test-only and bounded, with negligible fixed allocation and no product-path impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Checked synchronous UI/layout work, selector invalidation scope, repeated work, retention, allocation, and expensive-boundary fan-out. The production CSS adds bounded local layout to existing virtualized badges; the fixture is fixed-size test-only work. No valid performance findings or regression-fix learning signal.
